criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the YED-227 decisions against the runtime-ledger helper and found two spec-1 mismatches: direct-path overmatching in `_resolve()` (line 126) and lack of an exclusivity check for append-only writers (line 156). The intended fix is present in spirit, but these are real behavior gaps, so this stays below the pass line.

The patch includes both implementation changes and targeted selftests for append-only, read-only, typo, mixed append/read, and a live-repo guard. I checked the changed files for TODOs and missing load-bearing pieces; none stood out. The acceptance-oriented coverage is mostly there, with only a thin edge on end-to-end graph verification.

File placement under `.claude/hooks/` and `.claude/scripts/` is correct, the shared-helper import is localized, and I did not find an alex-prefixed project-skill naming violation or an obvious house-rule break. The change is conventional for this repo.

The change adds one shared helper instead of duplicating the rule in two places, and it avoids placeholder-ledger behavior. I did not see tombstoned-decision resurrection, fabricated metric surfaces, or other major anti-patterns.

The new selftests emit explicit pass/fail reporting and the code comments explain the intended contract well. The remaining issue is the docstring/comment overclaim at line 80, which is a minor honesty/traceability blemish.

defects.quote: lit = set(n for n in NAME_RE.findall(target) if "artifacts" in target or target.startswith(".claude"))
defects.description: This accepts any target string containing an artifacts path and then whitelists the basename, so a writer to `.claude/artifacts/sub/foo.jsonl` would incorrectly excuse the direct ref `.claude/artifacts/foo.jsonl`. Decision 1 only allows skips for refs directly under `.claude/artifacts/`.

The helper only accumulates names from append-mode writes and never checks for other tracked writers that also touch the same ledger in non-append mode. That means a ledger with one append writer plus an overwrite/truncate writer is still treated as runtime-created, contradicting the requirement that the ledger be written only in append mode.
